clue.text: Unspectacular flag on marsh

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing placed on another comes after it, so the first-named piece is written second

blocks.note: a bog is wet marshy ground
a standard is a banner or flag

explanation.surface: A dull-looking flag planted on a stretch of marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'flag on marsh' puts the flag after the marsh. Bog-standard is British slang for ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog-standard is informal British slang for something basic and ordinary, with nothing special about it.

clue.text: Opening provided to invest in gold and diamonds

indicators.note: to invest something in a place is to put it inside, so one piece is placed within the others

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
provided that means on condition, as does if
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A financial opportunity to put money into gold and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'opening' as a business opportunity; here it is a hole. OR and ICE together hold IF.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or aperture, especially in the body, so it is an opening.

clue.text: Round leader in parliament, Charles I scattered guards

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept
things scattered are thrown about in disorder, so these letters are rearranged
a guard stands around what it protects, so the shuffled letters surround the single letter

blocks.note: the first letter of parliament
taken as written, the king and his numeral

explanation.surface: Charles I, scattering his guards, faces the Round(head) leader in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Civil War between Charles I and Parliament's Roundheads; 'Round' is in fact the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spherical means shaped like a ball, which is one sense of the adjective round.

clue.text: Just over four weeks: a male finally out of danger

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
out of here means taken away from, so a letter is removed from the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of male
peril is a synonym for danger

explanation.surface: A man coming through four weeks of danger safely.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of male is taken out of PERIL, and A goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: April has thirty days, a little more than four seven-day weeks, so it is a month just over four weeks long.

clue.text: Dead skilful cushioning punch internally

indicators.note: a cushion surrounds and softens what it holds, so one word wraps around the other
internally means only the inside, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: deft means skilful and nimble
the inner letters of punch

explanation.surface: A boxer deftly softening a punch so it lands dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Defunct means no longer existing or functioning, a synonym of dead.

clue.text: Ridiculous bug has overwhelmed relative

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the first word swallows the second inside it

blocks.note: to bug someone is to annoy or rile them
sib is short for sibling

explanation.surface: An insect has got the better of a family member, which is laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug looks like an insect but is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means provoking laughter, especially scornful laughter, so it is a synonym of ridiculous.

clue.text: Focus of interest US money, balance required on time

blocks.note: a cent is a coin in American currency
the rest is the balance or remainder
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An accountant's note that the US funds balance is needed on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Centre stage is the most prominent position, the place where attention is concentrated.

clue.text: Kept up by bonehead, negative plan

indicators.note: kept by means held within the following words, so the letters are lying inside them
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A stupid person and a negative attitude hold up a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters ADNEGA read upwards give AGENDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of things to be done, or more loosely a scheme or plan someone is pursuing.

clue.text: Language in foreign glen I don't speak!

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A traveller in a strange valley who can't speak the local tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'I don't speak' a language that turns out to be English itself.
explanation.definitionFit: English is the language of England and many other countries.

clue.text: Turn one's nose up at garbage

blocks.note: first meaning: to decline or reject, a verb stressed on the second syllable
second meaning: rubbish, a noun stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone sniffily looking down on a pile of rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling serves as a verb meaning decline and a noun meaning waste matter.

clue.text: Top taste, we suspect, with old vegetable

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious and not as it should be, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A food critic doubts that an old vegetable can offer top taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet potato is a tropical root vegetable with orange flesh.

clue.text: North African city, more spicy

blocks.note: first meaning: the Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar
second meaning: the comparative of an adjective for sharp flavour

explanation.surface: A Moroccan city whose food is hotter than most.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan port shares its spelling with the comparative of tangy, sharper or more piquant.

clue.text: Pine front for yew weapon?

blocks.note: to pine is to long or yearn
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: Pine wood used for the front of something made of yew.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine and yew both look like trees, but pine is the verb meaning yearn. The question mark flags that yew weapon is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The English longbow was traditionally carved from yew, so it is the classic weapon made of that wood.

clue.text: Raise head on effectively having missed alarm call?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of effectively
someone who sleeps through the alarm ends up behind time

explanation.surface: Getting up and lifting your head after oversleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Raise looks like getting out of bed, but it means lift in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to lift their spirits, so raise works in the sense of cheer up.

clue.text: Worry about garden party, hosting one where grounds will be soaked?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around what follows
a host has guests inside, so the outer word holds the next piece too

blocks.note: care is anxiety or worry
a fête is an outdoor fundraising party, often in a garden
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fretting that rain will soak the lawn at a garden party.
explanation.walkthrough: Grounds looks like the garden but means coffee grounds; CARE holds both FETE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafetière is a plunger coffee pot in which ground coffee steeps in hot water.

clue.text: Number embracing country ceremony

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the first word wraps around the second

blocks.note: forty is a number
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Many people from a country hugging at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A formality is an observance done for the sake of convention, much like a ceremony.

clue.text: Sailor accepting work, figure a good wage?

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the first word holds the others within it

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
op is short for opus, a work
a doll is a small human figure

explanation.surface: A sailor taking on work and reckoning up a decent wage.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure looks like a sum of money but means a small model person.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dollar is the highest price or pay, so a good wage is an example of it.

clue.text: Clause for and against one, thus

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
v is short for versus
I is the Roman numeral one
so and thus both mean in this way

explanation.surface: A contract clause argued for and against by one party.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement, typically a clause beginning 'provided that'.

clue.text: Time to put out dog, originally neglected

indicators.note: originally points to how the word begins, so only its first letter is used
put out can mean disturbed or knocked out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of dog

explanation.surface: An owner reminded that it's time to let the dog out, having forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out or not done, the same as neglected.

clue.text: Upset — and in pieces?

blocks.note: first meaning: emotionally distressed, an informal phrase
second meaning: literally sliced into bits

explanation.surface: Someone so distressed they are falling to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut up is informal for being upset, while literally it means chopped into pieces.

clue.text: Given copper plating, detest a castle

indicators.note: plating is a thin outer coat, so the metal covers what is inside it

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
hate is a synonym of detest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes a castle given a copper finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French castle or large country house.

clue.text: Protection for head which has squeezed in

indicators.note: to squeeze something in is to press it inside, so the second word goes within the first

blocks.note: that and which are both relative pronouns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Headgear that has been crammed on tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin hat is a soldier's steel helmet, worn to protect the head.

clue.text: Reasonable plate of slime?

blocks.note: goo is sticky slime
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plate of slime is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: a GOO DISH is a plate of slime.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodish means fairly good, acceptable without being excellent, so reasonable.

clue.text: Some time without love on North American lake

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: an hour is a period of time
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spending some time alone and loveless on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Huron is one of the five Great Lakes on the US–Canada border.

clue.text: Cooker isn't switched on

indicators.note: to switch is to swap around, so these letters change places

blocks.note: an Aga is a British range cooker brand
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that the stove has not been turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched on' reads as a phrase, but on is the definition. An Aga is a heavy cast-iron cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Against and on can both mean in contact with, as in leaning against or on a wall.

clue.text: Feeling resentment, drink

blocks.note: first meaning: aggrieved and resentful
second meaning: a British pale ale with a strong hop flavour

explanation.surface: A resentful person turning to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is the British name for a well-hopped draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means resentful, and the noun is a type of beer served in British pubs.

clue.text: Wrong I can't put right, accommodating old lover

indicators.note: putting something right means rearranging it into proper order, so these letters are reworked
to accommodate is to give room to, so the shuffled letters hold another piece inside

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they can't make amends with a former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrong reads as a noun to be put right, but it is the adjective defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means not precise or accurate, so it can serve for wrong in the sense of incorrect.

clue.text: Cooking ingredient, gluey drops plastered round end of spoon?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
plastered is slang for drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order
round means surrounding, so the reworked letters go around the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of spoon

explanation.surface: Sticky drips smeared around a spoon after measuring out a sweet ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Golden syrup is a thick pale-gold British sugar syrup, used much like corn syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup is used in baking and puddings, so it is a cooking ingredient.
